title: Bern-Barcelona EEG database: focal and nonfocal intracranial EEG signal pairs (Andrzejak, Schindler & Rummel 2012)
description: The Bern-Barcelona EEG database contains 7500 pairs of 20-second intracranial EEG signals (3750 focal and 3750 non-focal), sampled at 512 Hz, from five patients with pharmacoresistant temporal lobe epilepsy. The pairs were drawn from interictal recordings of presurgical long-term monitoring. This BIDS version is a lossless repackaging of the published text files into BrainVision format. Patient, channel and time of origin were not stored, so all runs are pooled under a single pseudo-subject.
methods_description: Long-term intracranial EEG was recorded with AD-TECH strip and depth electrodes at the University of Bern. The signals were band-pass filtered at 0.5-150 Hz (zero-phase Butterworth), down-sampled to 512 Hz where needed, and re-referenced to the median of artifact-free channels. Focal channels were defined as those showing the first ictal changes, judged by visual inspection. Signal pairs of neighbouring channels were randomly drawn from 20-s windows, excluding seizures and the three hours after the last seizure. Pairs with prominent artifacts were discarded.
